purpose: Persistent promotion ledger for research signals, infrastructure findings and data-quality blockers so promising evidence is not forgotten or silently promoted.

governance.reviewRule: On substantial BUY Radar research work, inspect this register and the linked current evidence. If a review trigger is met, surface it to the user and propose the next validation step. Never silently promote a signal.

signals.title: BTC payout-address pattern for NON-Easy NiceHash blocks
signals.hypothesis: Repeated NiceHash pool coinbase payout addresses may help distinguish operational/non-EasyMining blocks from EasyMining player payout addresses, but an address must never be the sole classifier.

explicitNonEasyExamples.evidence: User-provided NiceHash LOTTERY UI showed 'BTC reward found for NON easy order' and the payoutAddress.

currentEvidenceSnapshot.interpretation: Strong pattern worth tracking; not enough to assert NON-Easy from address alone.

blockingIssues: Only one explicit NON-Easy UI example is currently registered.
Absence from public singleReward is not proof of NON-EasyMining.
Payout addresses may rotate, be reused or serve more than one operational purpose.
reviewTriggers: At least five explicit NON-Easy product-level examples across distinct BTC block heights are captured.
The repeated payout address has at least twenty independently observed NiceHash pool blocks and zero exact EasyMining-confirmed matches in the same evidence set.
A new explicit NON-Easy source or public endpoint becomes available.

toCandidate: At least five explicit NON-Easy product-level confirmations support the same address-pattern hypothesis.
No contradictory exact EasyMining product evidence is present for the candidate address pattern.
The address pattern is evaluated as supporting evidence only, never as a sole classifier.
toValidated: A held-out set shows the pattern separates explicit NON-Easy from EasyMining-confirmed blocks without identity leakage.
Performance is reported with false-positive counts and address-rotation limitations.
toProductionEligible: Any use is limited to attribution/data-quality support unless separate causal evidence shows incremental pre-entry BUY value.
A dedicated baseline comparison and rollback plan pass.

signals.nextReviewWhen: Any review trigger is met, or a new explicit NON-Easy example is captured.

signals.title: Public market pricing-lag / work-per-native edge
signals.hypothesis: A pre-registered divergence between public market conditions and EasyMining ticket work-per-native cost may contain incremental pre-entry information.
blockingIssues: Raw market price denomination and executable all-in buyer price are not independently verified.
Walk-forward labels remain insufficient.
Difficulty/hashrate input disagreements remain a separate unresolved data-quality issue.
Forward quote movement is not realized ticket ROI or HIT/MISS performance.
reviewTriggers: research/lag-report.json no longer reports only INSUFFICIENT_LABELS for the pre-registered walk-forward evaluation.
Raw market price denomination/executable price semantics are independently verified.
Authorized order-level outcomes become sufficient for an out-of-sample incremental-value test.

toCandidate: The pre-registered lag hypothesis has evaluable causal walk-forward labels.
Price/unit semantics required by the hypothesis are independently resolved.
No material time-leakage or stale-source integrity blocker remains.
toValidated: Out-of-sample comparison shows incremental value beyond the existing EV model.
Order-level HIT/MISS or realized ROI evidence supports the same direction without retrospective threshold fitting.
Losses, costs, uncertainty and clustered market episodes are reported.
toProductionEligible: Shadow comparison against the frozen baseline succeeds under the current relay/model regime.
No deterioration of calibration, safety guards or alert quality is observed.

signals.nextReviewWhen: Walk-forward evidence becomes evaluable, pricing semantics are resolved, or enough authorized order-level outcomes accumulate.

signals.title: Palladium S 60-minute momentum candidate
signals.hypothesis: A frozen four-factor 60-minute pre-entry momentum pattern may separate better Palladium S entries from non-matches.
blockingIssues: Prospective performance gate has not yet been demonstrated as satisfied.
Historical hypothesis-origin evidence is excluded from prospective validation.
Merged-mining math/input provenance issues must not be hidden by candidate performance.
reviewTriggers: Prospective eligible Palladium S order count reaches 30.
Prospective Palladium S HIT count reaches 3.
The frozen candidate evaluator reports enough outcomes for its first performance claim.

toValidated: At least 30 eligible prospective orders and at least 3 prospective HITs are available, per the frozen candidate registration.
CORE_MATCH versus not-CORE_MATCH performance is evaluated without changing the frozen rules.
Causal pre-entry guards and same-relay requirements pass.
toProductionEligible: The candidate adds incremental value over the existing production decision baseline.
A shadow rollout shows no safety/calibration regression and includes a rollback plan.

signals.nextReviewWhen: The frozen prospective evaluator reaches its registered 30-order and 3-HIT minimums.

signals.title: Five-minute phone delivery path
signals.hypothesis: Hourly phone checks may miss materially useful short PRIMARY BUY NOW/STRONG BUY windows.
blockingIssues: The registered minimum is three resolved strict windows; only two are currently resolved.
reviewTriggers: resolvedWindowCount reaches at least 3.
fiveMinutePushRecommended changes to true.

toValidated: Existing alert-latency policy recommends the five-minute path using its pre-registered thresholds.
toProductionEligible: Delivery-path implementation is tested independently of BUY decision logic.
No duplicate-alert or notification-storm regression is introduced.

signals.nextReviewWhen: The third resolved qualifying window appears or the report recommendation changes.

signals.title: Difficulty/hashrate input reconciliation
signals.hypothesis: Material feed-vs-difficulty model disagreement should be explained by verified upstream conventions before difficulty-derived estimates can be promoted.
blockingIssues: Upstream difficulty convention is not independently verified.
Network hashrate estimates and difficulty-derived work can legitimately reflect different estimation windows.
A MATH PASS is consistency, not proof of external input truth.
reviewTriggers: Upstream difficulty/network-hashrate field semantics are independently verified from authoritative source behavior.
A persistent disagreement changes materially after verified input normalization.
A proposed BUY feature depends on difficulty-derived EV.

toValidated: Field semantics, units, freshness and chain-specific difficulty conventions are independently verified.
The remaining disagreement is quantitatively explained and reproducible.
No unsupported chain receives a 2^32 difficulty conversion.
toProductionEligible: Any production use passes shadow comparison without weakening existing WARNING/CRITICAL safeguards.

signals.nextReviewWhen: Authoritative upstream semantics are verified or a candidate depends on these inputs.

signals.title: Reward-event multiplicity versus winning-order outcome
signals.hypothesis: Order-level HIT/MISS and reward/event multiplicity are different units. One winning order can produce many reward records/events, especially on high-block-frequency chains such as KAS/Titanium, so reward counts must never substitute for winning-order counts.

currentEvidenceSnapshot.highFrequencyChainExample: KAS/Titanium can produce many rewards from one winning order.
currentEvidenceSnapshot.implementationGuard: A binary HIT no longer synthesizes rewardCount=1 when multiplicity is unavailable.

blockingIssues: Exact semantics of source-specific reward counters are not independently verified across every source.
Merged-mining payout legs, reward records and successful block events may be different units.
Existing HIT/MISS-only safe batches often do not contain explicit reward multiplicity.
reviewTriggers: A source contract or authoritative documentation defines reward-count semantics for an order source.
Authorized order-level outcomes include explicit reward multiplicity and complete payout data.
A KAS/Titanium reward-intensity analysis is proposed for calibration.

toValidated: Each reward-count source used in analysis has an explicit verified unit.
Binary HIT/MISS remains one completed order per exposure regardless of reward multiplicity.
Missing multiplicity remains unavailable and is never synthesized from a HIT.
toProductionEligible: This item is a semantic guardrail, not a BUY feature; any production use is limited to enforcing unit separation in reports and calibration.
All relevant regression tests and aggregate-report checks pass without changing CURRENT/BUY decisions.

signals.nextReviewWhen: Reward-count source semantics are verified or reward intensity is proposed as a model/calibration feature.

signals.title: Completed-order denominator and lifecycle censoring
signals.hypothesis: Only verified COMPLETED orders should supply the ordinary HIT/MISS denominator. Explicit CANCELLED, EXPIRED or other non-COMPLETED rows are censored exposures and must not be converted into MISS.
blockingIssues: Earlier sanitized global batches did not preserve lifecycle status.
Source-specific meanings of expired/pending/error lifecycle states are not independently verified.
Partial-duration cancelled tickets may have different exposure and refund semantics from completed orders.
reviewTriggers: A future authorized order source preserves explicit lifecycle status.
Legacy batches are re-exported or independently verified with lifecycle state.
A proposed performance claim depends materially on rows whose lifecycle status is unknown.

toValidated: Explicit non-COMPLETED lifecycle states are consistently censored from HIT/MISS calibration.
Confidence calculations use only lifecycle-verified COMPLETED known outcomes.
Legacy unknown-status rows cannot silently become confidence-eligible.
toProductionEligible: This item is a correctness guardrail rather than a BUY feature; production use is limited to denominator integrity.
Regression tests and safety guards pass without changing CURRENT/BUY thresholds.

signals.nextReviewWhen: A source with explicit lifecycle status is used for global calibration or legacy lifecycle can be independently verified.

signals.title: Palladium M aggregate signal-outcome validation
signals.hypothesis: Periods dominated by favorable Palladium M Radar states may show better global completed-order outcome rates than WAIT-dominated periods.
blockingIssues: Daily/monthly aggregates do not identify the exact entry signal seen by each order.
Reward-to-winning-order mapping must be independently verified before reward counts can become HIT counts.
Reward timestamp versus order-cohort bucketing semantics are not yet verified.
Lifecycle scope must be COMPLETED only; cancelled/expired exposures are censored.
Timezone used by aggregate outcome data must match the exposure reconstruction.
reviewTriggers: A complete month of Palladium M COMPLETED aggregate outcomes is available with explicit timezone and verified reward semantics.
At least five GOOD-dominant and five WAIT-dominant aggregate-eligible days are available.
Authorized order-level Palladium M outcomes become available for direct entry-time validation.

toCandidate: The aggregate protocol is evaluated on held-out periods without changing its frozen thresholds.
GOOD-dominant versus WAIT-dominant outcome direction is stable across more than one calendar period.
No lifecycle, reward-unit, timezone or reward-bucketing blocker remains for the compared periods.
toValidated: Order-level or equivalent causal evidence confirms the same direction seen in aggregate validation.
Package-normalized baseline and model-expected hit rates are reported with uncertainty.
The result remains stable under reasonable day-boundary and coverage sensitivity checks.
toProductionEligible: A dedicated shadow comparison shows incremental value over the frozen CURRENT baseline.
No safety, calibration or alert-quality regression is observed.

signals.nextReviewWhen: A complete Palladium M aggregate outcome month is available or direct order-level causal outcomes become available.
